conviction_note: Against an 11.65% implied move and a -7.35 call-bid skew I found nothing that changes the RPO/capex debate that dominates the night, but two specific dated facts the previews do not carry - the entire $20bn equity leg of Oracle's own funding plan is still unissued with the syndicate quietly widened on 23 June, and the gas pipeline to the Project Jupiter OpenAI site was pushed to Feb 2027 after a second state permit denial - both tilt modestly against a market positioned for a bounce, so a small negative well inside the straddle rather than a directional call on the print.

findings.finding: Oracle has sold ZERO shares under its $20bn at-the-market common equity program: the FY2026 10-K tags 'Common stock shares sold' under the ATM Offering member as 0, and the FY2026 cash flow statement shows only $1,449m of common stock proceeds (ESPP/option exercises) against $4,954m of mandatory convertible preferred and $46,093m of notes/term loans - yet on 2026-06-23, one day after filing the 10-K, Oracle filed a 424B5 adding roughly ten further sales agents to that same $20bn program, and shares outstanding are still ~2.88bn (2,880,471,000 at 2026-06-12), so the whole ~127m-share, 4.4%-of-shares-out supply is still to come and the Q1 10-Q filed with this print is its first disclosure window.
findings.why_not_priced: The February plan was received as financing solved - CDS tightened sharply the day it was announced (CNBC, 2026-02-02) - and since then the $20bn ATM has only ever been referenced as an intention inside the FY2027 '$40bn of debt and equity' line, never as unexecuted supply. If the market were pricing 127m shares of imminent issuance into this print you would not see a -7.35 vol-point call-bid skew, a 0.79 put/call open-interest ratio and a 37% rally off the 24-July level of $114.99 (the price stamped in Oracle's own 2026-07-28 Form 4) with the stock closing the gap back to where the Vice Chairman sold in late June at $156-165. Equity issuance is the one mechanism that mechanically caps an up-tail, and a company that has just recovered 37% and must fund ~$90-95bn of gross FY2027 capex against $31.98bn of operating cash flow has both the motive and, as of 23 June, the expanded distribution machinery to sell into strength immediately after this print. This is a cluster: the R70 tag, the R8 cash flow line and the R1 share count are three readings of one document (the FY2026 10-K) and should count once; the 424B5 agent expansion is the genuinely separate leg.
findings.independence: The 2026-06-23 424B5 adding sales agents to the same program is a separate filing from the 10-K and is what you file before distributing size: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001341439/000119312526278585/d120346d424b5.htm . Separately, S&P's 2026-07-09 downgrade to BBB-/A-3 models FY2027 capex at $90-95bn versus its own prior $60bn forecast, which is the funding hole the equity leg exists to fill: https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/sourceId/101695609

findings.finding: The Green Chile gas pipeline that is to fuel Project Jupiter - the Oracle/OpenAI Stargate campus in Dona Ana County, New Mexico that Oracle itself promoted on 2026-07-28 and that is designed around ~2.5GW of Bloom Energy gas fuel cells - has been pushed from 15 August 2026 to 1 February 2027 in an Energy Transfer/Transwestern filing, after the New Mexico State Land Office denied the route permit for a second time on water-use and emissions grounds.
findings.why_not_priced: This lives in FERC/pipeline and New Mexico local press, not in equity research: the sell-side preview for this print is entirely RPO, OCI growth and capex, and the delay was never carried by the wire services that feed the previews. It is also a regulatory refusal by a state land commissioner - twice - rather than a supply-chain slip, so it is not fixable on Oracle's own timetable, which is the opposite of the framing Oracle used on 2026-03-06 when it rebutted the Abilene stories by saying no sites required to meet contractual commitments were delayed. If the market had priced power availability as the binding constraint on the 12% twelve-month RPO conversion guide, a 37% rally off the July low on ChatGPT-6 sentiment would not have happened without a single preview asking about Jupiter's first-power date. Note it cuts mostly at FY2028 rather than FY2027, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Confirmed independently by the trade press with the date in the URL path: https://www.energyconnects.com/news/gas-lng/2026/august/gas-pipeline-for-proposed-oracle-data-center-delayed-to-2027/ . Oracle's own 2026-07-28 release promoting the site sets the baseline expectation it cuts against: https://www.oracle.com/news/announcement/project-jupiter-2026-07-28/

searched_and_found_nothing: Depreciation / useful life lever: pulled the actual 10-K numbers (depreciation $7,623m FY2026 vs $3,867m FY2025 vs $3,129m FY2024; servers and networking equipment at a 6-year life, unchanged) - the step-up is real and large but it is THE most-written-about thing at Oracle in 2026 (Burry, footnotesanalyst, every hyperscaler-depreciation piece) and Oracle's non-GAAP already includes it, so I could not write an honest why_not_priced. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1341439/000119312526277521/R50.htm

Headcount / margin lever: 10-K shows 141,000 employees at 2026-05-31, down 21,000 (13%) y/y, with WARN last-work-days clustered 30 May - 15 June 2026, so Q1 FY2027 is the first full-benefit quarter against a consensus EPS of ~$1.73 sitting at the bottom of Oracle's own $1.72-1.76 guide. Genuinely a positive asymmetry, but it was covered on 2026-06-23 and EPS is demonstrably not what moves this stock (the June print fell 8.5% on a beat). https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/oracle-cuts-21-000-jobs-124728934.html

Second layoff round: Business Insider reported 2026-08-11 that managers were told to draw up lists ahead of the 1 September fiscal Q2 start, some teams facing double-digit cuts - already picked up by Yahoo, Quartz, TheStreet and the HR trades, so covered, and the restructuring charge would land in Q2 not Q1. https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/oracle-planning-round-layoffs-august-134527039.html

FX: dollar is roughly 1% weaker than at the 10 June guidance date (DXY just under 100 on 2026-06-10 versus 98.75 on 2026-09-10) - a real mechanical tailwind to a guide given at then-current rates, but I could not source a clean June 10 close and the effect is a few tenths of a point on revenue, below the noise floor here.
New megadeal / RPO surprise: searched for any large OCI contract signed June-August 2026 (Meta, xAI, Anthropic, sovereigns) that would spike RPO again - found nothing announced in the window.
Fresh 8-Ks: EDGAR shows no 8-K after 2026-06-10, so no quiet disclosure between the prints.

Insider cluster: only Form 4s are Jeff Henley (Vice Chairman) selling 340,540 shares at $156-165 on 2026-06-24 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-01-02, taking direct holdings to zero, and a 523-share RSU dividend accrual for the CLO - estate-planning shaped, not a signal.
Oracle Health / Cerner erosion: KLAS 2026 shows Oracle Health shedding 56 acute-care hospitals in 2025 while Epic added 77, third straight year of losses - real, slow, and published in May 2026.
S&P BBB-/A-3 downgrade (2026-07-09), CDS at ~214bp, the $300bn OpenAI concentration and OpenAI's own $122bn March raise - all heavily covered and, on a stock 52% off its high, plainly in the price.

Off-balance-sheet / SPV project finance for the data centres: found the ~$18bn New Mexico package and Oracle's public comment that partners have diversified capital sources, but no closing or new structure disclosed in the June-August window that I could date.
Oracle newsroom (oracle.com/news) returned 403; worked around it via EDGAR and investor.oracle.com.
baseline_tension: Both findings cut against the baseline: the skew is the most call-bid in the universe and the stock has run 8.1% in five days and 37% off its 24-July level, while what I found is pending equity supply worth 4.4% of shares out and a state-permit power delay at a flagship OpenAI site - neither is in the run-up and neither is what the calls are paying for.
